title: The Curriculum Proof Gap: New Exams, Old Books, and the Dual AI Classroom
content:
Hi [Name],

A tension surfaced across education communities this week that many principals recognise immediately.

India's board pipeline is caught between ambition and infrastructure. The parliamentary panel flagged it plainly: CBSE curriculum aligns with NEP 2020 and NCF 2023, but NCERT textbooks for senior grades are still incomplete. Schools teach forward. Exams test application. Students hold old books — or expensive coaching notes filling a vacuum you did not create but must answer for.

At the same time, teacher AI tools accelerated. The new K-12 Educator plugin helps with planning and parent communication. Valuable. But student forums and faculty rooms tell a different story: polished output without explanation, take-home work losing authenticity, and quiet returns to supervised assessment.

Parents are not anti-AI. They are anti-opacity. Surveys this month show most families want personalization — and most cannot describe your AI rules, data practices, or proof standards.

Schools that rebuild trust will publish a Curriculum Proof Brief: what is taught, what is tested, which materials exist, and how student thinking is demonstrated in class — not assumed from submissions.

EduHexa has supported 100+ institutions through parent-trust building, board-season communication, and admissions messaging — with partners seeing up to 129% admission increases when public voice matched classroom reality.

Would you like our Curriculum Proof Brief template for this term?

Reply YES and we will share it.
excerpt: CBSE schools teach NEP-aligned curriculum and test application-based thinking while NCERT textbooks lag — and teacher AI tools accelerate as student proof standards fall behind. Schools need a Curriculum Proof Brief parents can verify.
